title-group.article-title: Anchor Recovery with Inclined Compressed Air Tunneling for the City Tunnel Leipzig

article-meta.author: Tim Babendererdea and Philipp Elsnerb
article-meta.aff: Babendererde Engineers, Markt 2, 23611 Bad Schwartau, Germany.

abstract.title: ABSTRACT
abstract.p: In the inner city of Leipzig, Germany, the London, U.K. based AMEC group, an international infrastructure specialist, faced the problem that old cable anchors from the construction pit of a multiplex shopping center built by AMEC in 1999/2000 had to be recovered from under existing buildings and the main shopping road. They were in the path of two tunnel boring machines (TBMs) prepared to build the so-called “City TunnelLeipzig”. To simply run over the anchors with the TBMs was not an option due to the risk of uncontrollable ground movement and face collapse directly under buildings. A recovery from the TBMs was technically and financially extremely risky. A recovery from the road was impossible as well as it would have had a major impact on the surrounding commerce. By chance a large building opposite to the shopping center was demolished in that time just over the area where some anchors crossed the tunnels, opening a short time window for surface works. The anchors were finally recovered by a pile borer and a slurry wall excavator in a first stage and by pipe jacking under compressed air along the anchor axis in a second stage.
Keywords: Pipe jack, Inclined, Compressed air, Anchor recovery.
